name: Calculation Fields
description: Adds spreadsheet-style form elements that evaluate an admin/developer-defined math expression over other fields and display the result live.
library_dependencies: math.js 11.11.1 (external CDN, cdnjs, client-side live evaluation)

suggests.drupal/webform: Enable the webform_calculation_fields submodule to use the calculation elements inside Webforms.

provides_plugin_types: Render element (FormElement) 'form_calculation_element' — a readonly number input that computes a result
Render element (FormElement) 'form_calculation_markup' — HTML markup that renders a computed result inside {{ }}
Webform element 'form_calculation_element' (WebformCalculationNumber, submodule) — number calculation element for webforms
Webform element 'form_calculation_markup' (WebformCalculationMarkup, submodule) — markup calculation element for webforms
project_description: Calculation Fields extends the Drupal Form API with two render elements, form_calculation_element (a readonly number input) and form_calculation_markup (HTML output), that evaluate a math expression such as ':quantity * :unit_price' over the values of other form fields, like a spreadsheet cell. Fields are referenced in the expression by their machine name prefixed with a colon, and an optional default can be supplied with a pipe (e.g. :discount|0). The result is computed live in the browser with the math.js library as the referenced fields change, and re-computed and re-validated server-side on submit with symfony/expression-language so a tampered client value cannot forge the stored result. The webform_calculation_fields submodule exposes the same two elements as Webform elements (Calculation Field and Calculation Markup) so site builders can add live calculators to webforms without code; calculation_fields_example and webform_calculation_fields_examples ship worked examples (quantity/price, BMI, loan repayment).
